From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Affordability check-in & pilot budget — ClearLedger

Samira — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same set of priorities and asks.

High-level pain / context
- Production search/chat feature experiencing large token variance peak during billing cycles; unit cost spikes unpredictably and is the largest line item in the feature P&L.
- Hard SLO requirement: p50 latency <200ms and p99 <500ms for live customer queries. Current setup is missing the tail.
- Security/compliance gating: SOC2 evidence + audit logs required for pilot procurement next month.

Goals you stated
1) Demonstrate a credible path to reduce per-conversation inference cost by >=35% within a 6–8 week pilot.
2) Keep end-user latency within SLOs while preserving answer quality (no visible regressions in sample prompts).
3) Produce an ops playbook (runbook + billing estimate) that your procurement/CFO can review.

Levers we discussed (pilot scope options)
- Lightweight: KV prefix caching + prefix-based batching (expect ~20–35% token-level reduction depending on query repeat rate).
- Standard: Batching + aggressive prefix+KV cache + model variant (mixed-precision quant) for CPU/GPU cost reductions (~35–50% typical).
- Experimental: Quantized 4-bit path with tuned kernels + advanced batching — higher risk, higher reward (50%+ cost upside in synthetic runs).

Immediate next steps
1) We will deliver a short pricing + pilot sizing workbook (attached) with two concrete options (conservative / accelerated) and assumptions by Friday. [Attachment: pilot-sizing-playbook.xlsx]
2) Rishi will run a quick cost simulation if you can share ~48–72 hours of query traffic (anonymized) to size batching gains.
3) Samira to confirm procurement timeline & security contact for SOC2 artifacts.
4) Book a 30-min follow-up with engineering to walk the pilot plan (I proposed Wed 11/3, 10:00–10:30 PT).

Attachments: redwood-pilot-pricing-overview.pdf (high-level pricing), pilot-sizing-playbook.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks — we’ll prioritize the conservative option first so procurement can evaluate low-risk numbers quickly.

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — helpful recap. Couple quick clarifying items from our side:

- Procurement/budget: CFO (Ben) is asking for a concrete head-to-head comparison: our current monthly cost for the feature vs expected monthly for the pilot options. He specifically wants a 1M-token and 10M-token baseline comparison, plus the expected payback window for any pilot investment.

Also — can you include an example ROI case where batching is enabled but we keep the same model variant? Ben wants to understand savings from batching alone vs batching + quantization.

Samira / Ben — quick note with illustrative numbers so you have something to take to procurement/CFO. These are estimates for planning; we will refine once we run a short simulation over your traffic.

Assumptions (example case)
- Avg tokens per interaction (prompt + answer): 1,200 tokens
- Baseline: current non-optimized path cost (model variant A) ≈ $2,200 per 1M tokens (includes model price + infra overhead in our sample setup)

Pilot option A — Batching + KV prefix cache (no quantization)
- Expected reduction: 30% token-equivalent savings on average (depends on query repeat rate)
- Example: effective cost ≈ $1,540 per 1M tokens (~30% lower)
- Primary value: reduces per-request tokens and improves throughput with minimal model changes

Pilot option B — Batching + KV cache + mixed-precision quantization
- Expected reduction: 45% token-equivalent / compute-cost savings in our bench runs
- Example: effective cost ≈ $1,210 per 1M tokens (~45% lower)
- Primary tradeoff: small, tunable risk to answer characteristics; we validate against your prompt set in the pilot.

Sample ROI framing (conservative)
- If you process 10M tokens/month and choose Option A, monthly cost goes from ~$22k to ~$15.4k (savings ≈ $6.6k/month). Pilot professional services and engineering integration expected to be 4–6 weeks and ~$8–12k one-time. Payback window ≈ 1.5 months with the above conservative numbers.

Batching-only impact vs batching + quantization
- Batching-only: primarily reduces wasted per-token compute by combining requests — helps throughput and cost if you can tolerate small added latency to aggregate.
- Batching + quant: compounds savings because both per-token compute and total tokens served are lower.

Security docs
- We can provide SOC2 Type II summary + audit contact + limited logs access for pilot review. DocS available: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPilotSheet

Next asks from our side
1) Please confirm you’ll share an anonymized 72-hour query dump (Rishi will use it) — email to rishi.malhotra@redwood.com.
2) Confirm procurement timeline and an ideal sign-by date so we can prioritize the conservative pricing in our materials.
3) I’ll schedule the 30-min follow-up (proposed Wed 11/3 10:00 PT) — let me know if that works.

If helpful I can also produce a one-page CFO memo summarizing assumptions and payback metrics.

--
